paper.title_en: Doubly heavy open--flavor tetraquarks within the relativistic quark model
paper.abstract_en: Mass spectra of the ground, orbitally and radially excited states of doubly heavy open--flavor tetraquarks are calculated within the relativistic quark model based on the quasipotential approach and quantum chromodynamics. Tetraquarks are considered as bound states of a heavy diquark $\mathrm{QQ^{\prime}}$ ($\mathrm{Q,Q^{\prime} = c,b}$) and a light antidiquark $\mathrm{\overline{qq^{\prime}}}$ ($\mathrm{q,q^{\prime} = u,d,s}$). The diquark--antidiquark interaction quasipotential includes both spin--independent and spin--dependent relativistic contributions. The finite sizes of the diquark and antidiquark are taken into account via the form factors of their interaction with gluons. Masses of the ground ($1S$) and excited ($1P$, $2S$, $1D$, $2P$, $3S$) states are calculated including the mixing of states with the same observable quantum numbers $J^{P}$ but different spins $S$. The obtained masses are compared with the lowest allowed thresholds for strong fall--apart decays into a pair of heavy--light mesons in $S$--wave. Most of the states lie significantly above these thresholds. However, several states, predominantly orbital excitations with large $J$, lie below or slightly above the corresponding thresholds and, thus, could be promising candidates for experimental observation. The number of such near--threshold states increases for tetraquarks containing bottom quarks. The predicted mass of the ground state of the $\mathrm{cc\overline{ud}}$ tetraquark with $J^{P}=1^{+}$ is consistent with the experimentally observed $\mathrm{T}_{\mathrm{cc}}(3875)^{+}$ state.
